title: FAR Out: every route into federal work for a small business, with the gates on each and where the opportunities appear
question: For a small business that wants federal work, what routes exist (direct contracts and set-asides, contract vehicles, SBIR/STTR and other R&D funding, Other Transactions and Commercial Solutions Openings, and work through primes and partners), what does each require, how does the government on the other side of the table actually buy, and what has changed in 2025-26 that the official pages have not caught up with?
venue: Commissioned guide — NOT PEER REVIEWED, NOT LEGAL OR COMPLIANCE ADVICE. Written by an AI research builder from public government sources for a public audience; every record links to its governing text. No affiliation with any firm or agency.
plain_abstract: FAR Out is a map for a small business trying to sell to the United States government. It starts by asking where you are, not yet registered, registered with no award, growing, holding a technology that needs funding, or looking for partners, and leads you to the routes that fit: set-asides and sole-source awards, the GSA Schedule and the big contract vehicles, SBIR and STTR and the other research programs, Other Transactions through consortia and the innovation front doors, and subcontracting, teaming, joint ventures and mentor-protégé arrangements. Each route carries what it requires, the gates you must clear first, the official text that governs it, and a saved search into a daily feed of open opportunities. A buyer's map explains how defense and civilian agencies plan and buy, and a dated page tracks what changed in 2025 and 2026, because much of it has. Written by an AI research builder from 1,427 public sources read as of 3 October 2026; not peer reviewed; not advice.
audience: the owner or business-development lead of a small business with no prior federal work, with a second layer for the experienced contractor; assumes no acquisition vocabulary
